data.narrative: Completed Module 3 'Risk-Based Ordering' learning about identifying risk types (integration, novelty, dependency, scale, business/legal), scoring uncertainty, front-loading high-risk items, using spikes to test assumptions, and planning around business blockers with stubbed interfaces.

dimension_scores.observation: Annotated 13 work items with risk scores (1-5) and types (Integration, Novelty, Dependency, Scale) distinguishing technical from business/legal risks
dimension_scores.evidence: artifacts/risk-plan-module-03.md contains risk annotations for all 13 items

dimension_scores.observation: Distinguished risk from dependency - auth is low-risk but high-dependency, built early to unblock risky items not because auth itself is risky
dimension_scores.evidence: module3_verification.md explicitly states 'Auth is low-risk, high-dependency. I put auth early not because it's risky, but because it unblocks risky items'

dimension_scores.observation: Identified Payment Processing as highest risk (5, Integration) and Availability Management as second highest (4, Novelty), front-loading these to retire biggest unknowns early
dimension_scores.evidence: Risk plan puts Availability Management (item 3) and Payment Processing (item 4) at top of build order

dimension_scores.observation: Created stubbed payment interface contract processPayment() with clear inputs/outputs, allowing team to continue work around business blocker
dimension_scores.evidence: Revised plan defines interface contract and stub implementation

dimension_scores.observation: Responded to business blocker (no Stripe account) by creating stubbed interface and revised build plan, escalated to PM with timeline request, identified 13 items team can continue while payments blocked
dimension_scores.evidence: module3_break.md and revised plan show business blocker handled with interface stub and team reassignment

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized that not all risks are technical - identified business/legal risk type separate from four technical categories, understood when to solve with code vs plan around with contracts
dimension_scores.evidence: module3_break.md identifies business blocker as non-technical risk requiring business solution, not code

strengths: Distinguished risk from dependency - foundational items vs risky items
Front-loaded high-risk items (availability concurrency, payment integration)
Created stubbed interface to continue work around business blocker
Recognized business/legal risks as separate from technical risks
data.recommendation: Use risk-ordered plan as foundation for Module 4 Vertical Slicing - each risk-retired item should be broken into smaller vertical slices that are buildable and testable increments

public_evidence.artifact: Risk-based build plan with business blocker handling
public_evidence.student_action: Annotated 13 work items with risk scores/types, ordered build plan to front-load high-risk items, created stubbed payment interface to handle business blocker (no Stripe account), escalated to PM
public_evidence.technical_detail: Plan distinguishes technical risks (integration, novelty, dependency, scale) from business/legal risks, defines processPayment() interface contract, identifies 13 items team can continue while payments blocked
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to identify and categorize risks, order work to retire unknowns early, and adapt plans around blockers using interface contracts and stubs

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Identified business/legal risk as separate category from integration, novelty, dependency, scale
Used 2-hour payment spike to test Stripe API before committing to full implementation
Defined processPayment() interface contract with stub implementation to allow development to continue around business blocker

learning_style_signals: prefers concrete examples and real-world scenarios
